Mobile Tree promotes subagent sessions to top-level rows when parent is in another worktree
Author
sdhector
Updated
16h ago
Labels
bug
area:sessions
platform:mobile
root-cause:found
Summary

On the mobile Tree view, a subagent session is rendered as a top-level row when its parent session is in a different worktree bucket. The data is correct: OpenCode stores parentID, and desktop/List views keep the session under its parent.

This is a display bug in the mobile Tree projection.

Reproduction
Create a parent session in a project root, for example /project.
Let it spawn a subagent that runs in a worktree, for example /project/worktree.
Open the mobile session sheet in Tree view.
The subagent appears as a top-level row under the worktree instead of under its parent. The parent row does not contain it.
Expected

A session with a parent that exists should never become a top-level Tree row. It should either:

be rendered under the parent's bucket, or
remain hidden behind the parent row.
Actual

MobileSessionsSheet.tsx groups children only within the current worktree bucket. Any child whose parent is outside that bucket is explicitly treated as a root:

ts
// Group children by parent within this bucket, and treat sessions whose parent
// is not in this bucket as top-level so nothing is hidden.
const idsInBucket = new Set(bucket.sessions.map((entry) => entry.id));
const bucketRoots = bucket.sessions.filter((entry) => {
  const parentId = getParentId(entry);
  return !parentId || !idsInBucket.has(parentId);
});

ts
// Group children by parent within this bucket, and treat sessions whose parent

Verified in 2.5.0 (6e3d996d) and current upstream main (2026-10-20).

Regression test

A focused source-level test using the exact predicate fails:

text
actual:   [ 'ses_child' ]
expected: []

The child is promoted to a root row solely because its parent is in another bucket.

Suggested fix

Use the global session graph when deciding roots, not only the current bucket. If the parent exists, attach the child to the parent's bucket or exclude it from the top-level list. Add a regression test with:

parent directory /project
child directory /project/worktree
child parentID pointing at the parent

Code path

Suggested fix direction matches the code that already exists: use the global id set / childrenBySessionId when deciding bucketRoots, keeping the bucket-local fallback only for parents that truly don't exist. The regression test you sketched (parent /project, child /project/worktree, cross-bucket parentID) targets the right predicate.
